title: CRU TS Monthly High-Resolution Gridded Climate Dataset (v4.10)
description: CRU TS (Climatic Research Unit gridded Time Series) is a monthly 0.5° grid of ten climate variables over all land areas except Antarctica, derived by interpolating monthly anomalies from weather-station observations with angular-distance weighting. Version 4.10 covers 1901–2025 and includes precipitation, mean/minimum/maximum temperature, diurnal temperature range, vapour pressure, cloud cover, wet-day and frost-day frequency and potential evapotranspiration, with per-cell station counts.
purpose: A long, station-based climate reference for Algeria back to 1901, widely used to compute drought indices (e.g. SPEI) and to evaluate reanalyses and satellite rainfall; the station-count field shows where values are actually supported by observations.

spatial_extent.description: All global land areas except Antarctica on a 0.5° grid. Algeria is covered; users subset it from the global files.

temporal_extent.description: v4.10 covers 1901–2025 (released 25 June 2026); the dataset is updated annually with a new version number.

variables.name: tmn / tmx
variables.description: Monthly average daily minimum / maximum temperature

variables.name: stn
variables.description: Number of stations supporting each cell value; 0 means the climatology was inserted

processing: Monthly station anomalies (relative to 1961–1990) are interpolated to the 0.5° grid with angular-distance weighting within a variable-specific correlation decay distance (e.g. 450 km for precipitation, 1200 km for temperature) and converted to actual values with the CRU CL v1.0 climatology. Secondary variables are derived where observations are lacking; PET is computed with a Penman–Monteith formula. The interpolation algorithm is unchanged since v4.03; v4.10 adds 2025 CLIMAT/MCDW observations passed through CRU quality control.
validation: Harris et al. (2020) provide diagnostics (station counts per cell and time step) rather than a single accuracy figure, and caution that trend analysis should be restricted to well-observed regions or masked using the station counts.
limitations: Where no station lies within the correlation decay distance, the value is replaced by the 1961–1990 climatology (Harris et al. 2020), which suppresses variability; this is likely over large parts of the Algerian Sahara and should be checked with the 'stn' field.
The number and location of contributing stations change over time, which can introduce artificial trends.

Secondary variables (vap, wet, cld) and derived variables (tmn, tmx, frs, pet) depend partly on precursor variables (Harris et al. 2020, Table 1), so they carry less independent observational information than pre, tmp and dtr.
At 0.5° (about 55 km) orographic rainfall in the Tell Atlas and Kabylie is smoothed.
No version DOI is available yet for v4.10 (CRU page: 'doi not yet available'); the CEDA archive currently holds v4.09.

algeria_notes: Northern Algeria has a reasonable station network in CRU TS, but the Sahara is sparsely observed; for southern Algeria inspect the station-count variable before interpreting anomalies or trends, since cells with zero stations carry the 1961–1990 climatology. CRU TS precipitation and PET are commonly used inputs to SPEI (see the existing speibase record).
